wholePhysicalScope: Queensland Heritage Register boundary 602256 and the mapped Mount Isa railway anchor the archaeological site. The register gives the south crusher group, adjacent north furnace foundations, the large vat to their west, four round vats to its north, and the northern works along the railway. Component spans and exact site positions use the registered sizes and approximate group positions.
lodDetails: Four authored levels retain the five surviving works, tall buttressed vat, four circular vats, ramp, flues, chimneys and low adobe. Near levels resolve open interiors, period castings, exposed brick, concrete rims and weathered fragments.
limitations: This is an exterior reconstruction of the documented archaeological remains of the Cloncurry treatment site. Equipment and the dimensions of the large vat, four round vats and three northern tanks follow the register. The present state is approximated from the documented remains and original terrain.

Individual footprints within the surveyed heritage boundary, excavation levels, surviving adobe course counts, debris, flue sections and fitting dimensions are estimates. The developed geometry reflects five surviving groups, with the roofs and full operating machinery omitted.

The published Qualla historical hero has conflicting recorded and current renditions, and the modern tank photograph requires attribution. No photograph or aerial imagery was adopted as a modeling reference.
